text:
alex: Heads-up — support just escalated a customer seeing intermittent 429s even though their quota shows available burst tokens. They say it started after a config deploy around 09:12 UTC.

maya: Curious — which limiter? global per-tenant or the new distributed tokenbucket?

alex: Distributed tokenbucket (v2) on prod region us-west-2. Support attached a short repro.

support-elena: Customer repro summary: 100 concurrent connections sending 50r/s each for ~30s, some requests succeed then ~25% get 429s. Their dashboard shows burst tokens remaining.


tj: Can you paste limiter logs (token events) for that tenant + timeframe?

alex: Pasting excerpt:

```
[09:12:18.123] limiter[tokenbucket] tenant=acct-42 instance=i-0a1 req_id=abc123 allow=true tokens_left=120
[09:12:18.124] limiter[tokenbucket] tenant=acct-42 instance=i-0b2 req_id=def456 allow=false tokens_left=0
[09:12:18.125] limiter[tokenbucket] tenant=acct-42 instance=i-0a1 req_id=ghi789 allow=false tokens_left=0
[09:12:18.130] refill[sync] tenant=acct-42 instance=i-0a1 added=50 next_refill=09:12:45
[09:12:18.130] refill[sync] tenant=acct-42 instance=i-0b2 added=0 note=skipped_conflict
```

alex: Notice i-0b2 logged "skipped_conflict" on refill. Looks like a race where one instance applied the refill and others aborted. But aborted instance still returned allow=false for earlier requests.

pat: Sounds like the leader election/refill locking failed to propagate. We had a refactor in v2 to optimistic refills with compare-and-swap on Redis keys. Could be a CAS retry edge-case.

oncall-bot: Deploy 09:11 UTC: limiter-service v2.3.4 -> v2.4.0 by ci/cd (alex).

maya: Repro locally? Try running two limiter instances against a fake Redis and hammer with the customer's pattern. If CAS races, we should see skipped_conflict logs.

alex: Repro script:```bash
# spin two instances (simulated) then run 100 concurrent clients
python tests/repro_tokenbucket_race.py --instances 2 --clients 100 --rate 50 --duration 30 --tenant acct-42
```

alex: Running repro on staging shows ~20% 429s with same skipped_conflict marker.


tj: Good. Root cause hypothesis: CAS loop returns stale read after another instance commits; our code treats CAS failure as "no refill" instead of retrying N times. Previously we retried up to 3 times; v2 removed retries to reduce latency.

pat: That explains it. Fix options: (A) reintroduce bounded retries for CAS, (B) switch refill to a single-leader with short lease, (C) central refill worker.

maya: Short-term mitigation: revert deploy to v2.3.4 (has retries) or patch v2.4.0 to add retries. Which is faster?

alex: Revert is fastest. Can we rollback? Oncall: can you queue rollback?

oncall-bot: Rollback requested by alex. Runbook step 3 requires approval from @pat.

pat: Approved. Rolling limiter-service back to v2.3.4 in us-west-2.

oncall-bot: Rollback started at 09:35 UTC.

alex: After rollback customer reports errors drop to <1% within 2 minutes.

support-elena: Customer confirmed mitigation works, thanks. Will keep monitoring and will not escalate further. :white_check_mark:


tj: Next: implement proper fix (A) with bounded retries and metrics for CAS failure rate. Also add an automated canary that runs the customer repro pattern on deploy for 5 minutes.

pat: Agreed. Action items: 1) tj implement retry patch + unit tests (due EOD tomorrow). 2) maya add canary job + alert on skipped_conflict > 1% during deploy. 3) alex write post-incident blameless summary.

alex: I'll draft the post-incident with timeline and include the repro script and logs.

maya: FYI also saw a secondary issue where refill timestamps sometimes skewed across instances due to clock drift in containers — add sync check to health probe.


tj: Will add a quick monotonic-timestamp check before applying refill.

pat: Great. We'll keep the rollback in place until patch + canary pass. Thanks everyone.

alex: One more note — customer asked about potential data loss; none occurred, only throttling. Confirmed no token state wiped.

support-elena: Customer PM replied with thanks and asked for ETA on permanent fix. I'll coordinate and update them once we have PRs.

alex: Closing thread for now, will post postmortem link when ready. :bow:
